42861015.abstract: PURPOSE: To quantify longitudinal changes in mesopic and scotopic retinal sensitivity (RS) and evaluate their relationship with retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) atrophy progression and foveal involvement in extensive macular atrophy with pseudodrusen-like appearance (EMAP). DESIGN: Retrospective longitudinal observational study. PARTICIPANTS: One hundred twenty-eight eyes from 66 patients with clinically confirmed EMAP followed at a tertiary inherited retinal diseases clinic. METHODS: Eyes with ≥1 visit including mesopic and red scotopic microperimetry using a validated 20-stimulus grid and multimodal imaging (blue autofluorescence and spectral-domain OCT) were included. Associations between square root-transformed RPE atrophy size and functional metrics (best-corrected visual acuity [BCVA], mesopic RS [mRS], and scotopic RS [sRS]) were analyzed using mixed-effects models adjusted for age and intereye correlation. Longitudinal rates of functional and structural change were estimated in eyes with ≥2 visits. Cox proportional hazards regression evaluated predictors of foveal involvement. MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Structure-function relationships, yearly rates of functional decline, and predictors of foveal involvement. RESULTS: Among 128 eyes (median age, 59.5 years; 69.7% female), larger RPE atrophy size was significantly associated with worse BCVA, mRS, and sRS (all P < 0.001), with the strongest association observed for paramacular mRS (R2m = 0.42). Forty-five eyes contributed to longitudinal analysis (median follow-up, 20.5 months). Retinal pigment epithelium atrophy enlarged linearly at 3.7 mm2/year, while mRS declined linearly at -1.3 dB/year. Best-corrected visual acuity and sRS demonstrated logarithmic decline patterns. Among eyes without baseline foveal involvement, faster macular mRS decline was the only significant predictor of subsequent foveal involvement (hazard ratio, 0.43 [95% confidence interval, 0.20-0.96]; P = 0.04), corresponding to a 133% increased risk per 1-dB decrease. CONCLUSIONS: In EMAP, mRS demonstrated stronger structure-function associations with RPE atrophy and a more consistent longitudinal decline than BCVA and sRS. Decline in macular mRS independently predicted subsequent foveal involvement, supporting microperimetry as a sensitive functional endpoint for patient stratification and interventional trials. FINANCIAL DISCLOSURES: Proprietary or commercial disclosure may be found in the Footnotes and Disclosures at the end of this article.
42861015.authors: Trinco A, Nardi C, D'Introno R et al.
42861015.title: Mesopic Microperimetry Captures Extensive Macular Atrophy with Pseudodrusen-Like Appearance Progression Beyond Visual Acuity: A Longitudinal Analysis.

42861385.abstract: PURPOSE: Biallelic EYS variants are one of the frequent causes of autosomal recessive inherited retinal disease worldwide, yet the EYS mutational landscape of Eastern European and Northern Asian populations has not been systematically described. We characterized the molecular and clinical spectrum of EYS-associated retinitis pigmentosa (RP) in this population. METHODS: Thirty-nine patients with confirmed biallelic EYS variants were selected from 500 patients enrolled in the prospective inherited retinal disease genotyping clinical trial (NCT03901391). All patients underwent whole exome sequencing with copy number/structural variant analysis and standardized ophthalmic phenotyping, including best corrected visual acuity (BCVA), slit lamp biomicroscopy, refractometry, perimetry, optical coherent tomography (OCT), fundus autofluorescence (FAF), ophthalmoscopy and electroretinogram (ERG). RESULTS: We identified 34 distinct EYS variants: 22 pathogenic, 8 likely pathogenic, and 4 variants of uncertain significance by American College of Medical Genetics (ACMG) criteria. Fifteen variants were novel, including eight structural deletions. Two recurrent alleles c.1155T>A (p.Cys385*) in 16 (20.3%) alleles, and c.8648_8655del (p.Thr2883Lysfs*4) in 15 (19.0%) alleles were the most frequent; together they accounted for 39.2% of alleles, with relatedness analysis supporting a shared founder origin. Median age of disease manifestation was 18 years and median BCVA 0.16 logMAR; worse acuity correlated with older age (rank correlation coefficient = 0.34, p = 0.035). CONCLUSION: This first description of the EYS spectrum in an Eastern European and Northern Asian cohort expands the allelic diversity of the gene, provides a genotype-phenotype description and defines two population-specific founder alleles amenable to targeted screening and future treatment.
42861385.authors: Weener M, Hatsenko I, Zolnikova I et al.
42861385.title: The mutational and clinical spectrum of EYS-associated retinitis pigmentosa in an Eastern European and Northern Asian cohort: two recurrent founder alleles.

42864617.abstract: BACKGROUND: Biallelic CFAP418 variants cause retinal degeneration with variable extraocular findings. The principal contribution of this familial case series is a comparison of four affected siblings carrying the same previously reported splice-donor variant, with explicit separation of original clinical records from recalled history and historical summaries. CASE PRESENTATION: Four Palestinian siblings from a consanguineous family had homozygosity for CFAP418 NM_177965.3:c.155 + 1G > A reported in a 2018 family research letter; a 2019 clinical laboratory report confirmed the variant in the older brother and sister and heterozygosity in both parents. At history collection in March 2026, the male twins reported an age of 27 years, their older brother 30 years and their sister 26 years. The twins, described by the family as monozygotic without independent zygosity confirmation, had congenital postaxial polydactyly; the other siblings did not. Dated records for the twins documented severe visual impairment, posterior subcapsular cataract, pigmentary retinal degeneration, macular outer-retinal abnormalities, markedly constricted Goldmann fields and virtually absent rod and mixed electroretinographic responses with residual cone responses. Acuity differed across visits and testing conditions. Contemporary standardized ophthalmic data were unavailable for the other two siblings. Participants reported photophobia, progressive visual difficulty and substantial effects on mobility, education, daily tasks and family roles. Documented care included ophthalmic and low-vision follow-up, optical-aid recommendations and supportive prescriptions; no measured treatment benefit was established. CONCLUSIONS: The family demonstrates a documented contrast in polydactyly alongside a shared molecular and retinal disease context. Recalled symptoms do not establish an electrophysiological transition between retinal diagnoses. The 2026 genotype-informed Bardet-Biedl diagnostic algorithm supports a syndromic interpretation across the sibship, while incomplete systemic ascertainment limits characterization of organ involvement. Standardized retinal follow-up, low-vision care, genetic counselling and multidisciplinary surveillance are warranted.
42864617.authors: Awad A, Gheith B, Harthiyyeh AA et al.
42864617.title: Intrafamilial phenotypic variation in four Palestinian siblings with CFAP418-related ciliopathy: a familial case series.

42866676.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To characterize peripheral retinal vascular alterations in USH2A-related retinitis pigmentosa (RP) using widefield OCT angiography (WF-OCTA) and to investigate their relationship with macular changes assessed by multimodal retinal imaging. DESIGN: Cross-sectional observational study. PARTICIPANTS: Thirty eyes of 30 patients with genetically confirmed USH2A-related RP and 30 age- and gender-matched healthy controls. METHODS: We performed complete ophthalmologic examination and multimodal retinal imaging, including fundus autofluorescence (FAF), OCT, OCTA, AF-based macular pigment optical density, and 130° WF-OCTA. A quantitative WF-OCTA analysis pipeline was developed to assess peripheral perfusion through concentric fovea-centered retinal rings. The Concentric Peripheral Perfusion Index, peripheral perfusion loss gradient, and perfusion profile slope were calculated. Associations between peripheral vascular status and central retinal imaging biomarkers were analyzed. MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: WF-OCTA perfusion quantitative metrics. RESULTS: Compared with controls, RP eyes showed significantly lower WF-OCTA perfusion indices across all eccentricity rings (all P < 0.05), with more pronounced perfusion loss in the outer retina and a steeper perfusion decline toward the periphery. Peripheral vascular impairment significantly correlated with visual field indices, preserved FAF area, retinal layer thicknesses, and macular vascular density, particularly at the intermediate capillary plexus. Eyes with bone spicule pigmentation or retinal vascular attenuation showed more severe peripheral vascular loss, whereas eyes with hyperautofluorescent ring demonstrated more preserved perfusion profiles. Autofluorescence-based macular pigment optical density values were reduced in RP and significantly associated with central vascular and structural parameters. Hyperreflective ganglion cell band was associated with more severe peripheral vascular impairment and worse macular vascular status. CONCLUSIONS: USH2A-related RP is characterized by marked peripheral retinal vascular rarefaction, more evident at increasing eccentricities and closely associated with central retinal structural, vascular, and pigmentary alterations. These findings support the concept of RP as a diffuse neurovascular retinal disorder extending beyond the outer retina. Quantitative WF-OCTA may provide clinically meaningful biomarkers for disease characterization and monitoring. FINANCIAL DISCLOSURES: Proprietary or commercial disclosure may be found in the Footnotes and Disclosures at the end of this article.
42866676.authors: Arrigo A, Forte G, Aragona E et al.
42866676.title: Peripheral Vascular Alterations in USH2A-Retinitis Pigmentosa and Relationship with Macular Involvement: A Cross-Sectional Study.

42866702.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To characterize short-term progressive loss of macular preserved autofluorescence (PAF) in choroideremia and to determine how baseline PAF morphology influences subsequent structural decline. DESIGN: Post hoc longitudinal analysis of a multicenter prospective natural history cohort (NIGHT study). PARTICIPANTS: A total of 106 participants (163 eyes) with genetically confirmed choroideremia and gradable fundus autofluorescence (FAF) imaging at baseline and month 12. METHODS: Regions of PAF were manually segmented on FAF images and converted into binary masks. Total PAF area and PAF perimeter were quantified at baseline and month 12 using an automated ImageJ based workflow. Associations between baseline characteristics (PAF area, perimeter, foveal status, and PAF region focality) and 12 months PAF change were evaluated using linear mixed effects models accounting for intereye correlation. MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Change in total macular PAF area over 12 months and its association with baseline PAF region characteristics. RESULTS: Mean PAF area decreased significantly from 3.77 ± 4.53 mm2 at baseline to 3.37 ± 4.11 mm2 at month 12 (mean change -0.41 ± 0.57 mm2; P < 0.001). Preserved autofluorescence region perimeter also declined significantly (-1.04 ± 2.56 mm; P < 0.001). In multivariable analysis, larger baseline PAF area (β = -0.071, P < 0.001) and greater baseline PAF region perimeter (β = -0.018, P = 0.003) were independently associated with greater PAF loss. In contrast, foveal preservation (P = 0.197) and PAF region focality (P = 0.569) were not significantly associated with progression. CONCLUSIONS: Macular PAF area measured by FAF demonstrated significant decline over 12 months in choroideremia and may represent a useful structural endpoint for assessing short-term disease progression. Larger baseline PAF area and perimeter were associated with greater subsequent PAF loss. These findings may improve understanding of disease natural history and inform the design of future clinical trials. FINANCIAL DISCLOSURES: Proprietary or commercial disclosure may be found in the Footnotes and Disclosures at the end of this article.
42866702.authors: Chujo S, Abbasgholizadeh R, Alhelaly M et al.
42866702.title: Progression of Macular Tissue Loss in Choroideremia and Its Association with Baseline Fundus Autofluorescence Morphology.

42877450.abstract: Photoreceptor degeneration leads to irreversible vision loss in numerous inherited retinal diseases. While gene therapy addresses specific mutations, cell replacement strategies offer a potentially broader solution applicable across multiple genetic causes. This review traces the evolution of retinal transplantation approaches, from early fetal tissue transplants to modern pluripotent stem cell-derived retinal organoids. The development of three-dimensional retinal organoids marked a significant advancement, providing transplantable tissue that maintains cellular architecture and relationships. Preclinical studies have demonstrated that transplanted organoids can develop mature photoreceptors with outer segments, form synaptic connections with host bipolar cells, restore light responsiveness in host retinal ganglion cells, and enable light-responsive behaviors in animal models. The first human clinical application using induced pluripotent stem cell-derived retinal organoids has demonstrated safety and stable graft survival over 2 years, with potential functional improvement in one patient at around 1 year after transplantation. Recent innovations include genome-edited retinal organoids with reduced competing bipolar cells, which enhance functional integration by increasing host-graft connectivity. While significant challenges remain, including increasing transplantation area, improving surgical techniques, optimizing patient selection, and addressing manufacturing and regulatory considerations, continued progress in this field may offer hope for some visual improvement in currently untreatable retinal degenerative conditions.
42877450.title: Regenerative therapies using pluripotent stem cell-derived retinal organoids.

42877765.abstract: PURPOSE: MP-004 is a novel small molecule under development as a non-invasive therapeutic for inherited retinal dystrophies (IRDs), including retinitis pigmentosa. MP-004 halts photoreceptor degeneration by modulating calcium dysregulation and oxidative stress, two critical pathways involved in IRDs. Here, we evaluated its ocular concentration and safety profile following topical administration in three animal species (mouse, rabbit, and pig). RESULTS: Formulation of MP-004 with 0.3% hyaluronic acid substantially enhanced retinal concentrations in mice compared to non-formulated compound (6.67 vs 1.27 µg/g at 4 h). MP-004 reached the retina in all species evaluated, with minimal systemic exposure. In mice, serum concentrations were below 5 ng/mL, while in rabbits, the compound was undetectable in blood and peripheral tissues 12 h post-dose. Interestingly, in rabbits the maximum serum concentration was 43.6 ng/mL with a half-life of 20 minutes, whereas the maximum retinal concentration was 387 ng/g and the half-life of 6.34 h. Seven-day repeated-dose toxicity studies in mice and rabbits showed no systemic or ocular toxicity. In rabbits, only transient ocular redness was observed following administration, with no evidence of corneal damage or systemic adverse effects. Hematological and biochemical parameters remained within normal limits in both species. Importantly, retinal and optic nerve concentrations remained detectable in rabbits 7 days after the final dose, while the compound had been systemically eliminated, supporting prolonged retention in target tissues. CONCLUSION: These findings demonstrate that MP-004 is well tolerated and achieves effective retinal concentrations via topical delivery, overcoming a major barrier in retinal drug development. The favorable pharmacokinetic and safety profile across species, including anatomically relevant models, supports the advancement of MP-004 toward regulatory preclinical studies and subsequently, its clinical translation as a non-invasive therapy for IRDs.
42877765.authors: Lara-López A, Rodríguez-Hidalgo M, Sarasola-Gastesi M et al.
42877765.title: Pharmacological and Safety Evaluation of the Small Molecule MP-004 Following Topical Ocular Administration for the Treatment of Inherited Retinal Dystrophies.

42877891.abstract: This abstract serves to report on the available evidence on the different retinal and visual prostheses for patients with retinitis pigmentosa and other vision-threatening disorders with additional discussion on the ethical implications of such devices. The PubMed, Google Scholar, ScienceDirect, and ClinicalTrials databases were the main resources used for the literature search. An extensive search was performed to identify relevant literature and clinical trials regarding the advances and status of retinal prostheses up to January 2025. Eight devices were found to be current and were ordered by stimulation location. Five have active clinical trials. There are 7 main ethical considerations identified in the literature. Future directions will be presented in the review. This manuscript provides an update on human visual prosthetics, both current and discontinued. While some devices have achieved visual perception in animals and/or humans, there are still challenges to address in the field. Future efforts are headed toward more biocompatible, safe, ethical, and efficacious devices.
42877891.title: An update on human visual prosthesis: The Claes H. Dohlman lecture 2025.

42878232.abstract: Variants in the transcription factor CRX cause a spectrum of retinal degenerative disorders including Leber congenital amaurosis 7 (LCA7). LCA7-associated variants exert a dominant effect in developing photoreceptor cells, leading to cellular dysfunction and poor to absent visual acuity in patients. Here, we dissect the allelic heterogeneity of LCA7 using multimodal single-cell gene expression and chromatin accessibility analysis of retinal organoids. We generated mature (240 day) retinal organoids from patient-derived iPSCs carrying missense (K88Q) and nonsense (T155fs) variants, as well as from CRISPR-corrected control lines. We show that these variants, while both causing LCA7, produce unique transcriptional changes in human photoreceptors. Furthermore, the K88Q variant causes aberrant chromatin accessibility at sites typically bound by non-photoreceptor retinal transcription factors, indicating a partial derangement of normal retinal cell fate programming. This work demonstrates the gene regulatory mechanisms of pathogenicity of two disease-causing CRX variants in human retinal cells.
42878232.authors: Mullin NK, Voigt AP, Lamba DA et al.
42878232.title: Gene regulatory behaviors of mutant CRX proteins demonstrated with late-stage human retinal organoids.

42878579.abstract: PURPOSE: A staphyloma-like morphology has been reported in eyes with retinitis pigmentosa (RP). We investigated retinal curvature in RP using widefield swept-source optical coherence tomography and explored the mechanisms underlying this abnormal morphology. METHODS: This retrospective study included 74 eyes with RP and 40 control eyes, all with axial lengths of 22 to 26 mm. The curvature of Bruch's membrane was analyzed in the central and peripheral regions of all eyes. In 37 RP eyes with an ellipsoid zone (EZ) length ≥ 1.5 mm, curvature was further evaluated in EZ-preserved and EZ-defected areas and across the EZ boundary. RESULTS: Central macular curvature was significantly steeper in RP eyes (-23.55 ± 17.56 × 10⁻5 µm⁻1) than in controls (-7.72 ± 6.46 × 10⁻5 µm⁻1), whereas the peripheral retina was significantly flatter in RP (-6.84 ± 10.18 × 10⁻5 µm⁻1, inferior) than in controls (-15.14 ± 4.76 × 10⁻5 µm⁻1). Curvature was steeper in EZ-preserved areas (-30.40 ± 24.34 × 10⁻5 µm⁻1) than in EZ-defected areas (-8.00 ± 6.40 × 10⁻5 µm⁻1). Around the EZ edge, curvature on the central side was significantly steeper than that on the peripheral side. CONCLUSIONS: In RP, retinal curvature flattens with photoreceptor degeneration, resulting in relatively steep concavity in the central macula or EZ-preserved regions. These findings suggest that photoreceptor loss contributes to secondary alterations in global retinal and ocular configuration.
42878579.authors: Yamabe Y, Fujibayashi S, Ichinohe H et al.
42878579.title: Retinal Flattening Associated With Photoreceptor Degeneration Leads to the Formation of Staphyloma-Like Morphology in Retinitis Pigmentosa.

42881268.title: Optogenetic therapy shows early promise for treating retinitis pigmentosa.

42883974.abstract: Retinal degenerative diseases, a broad group encompassing age-related macular degeneration (AMD) and various forms of inherited retinal disease (IRD), are among the leading causes of irreversible blindness worldwide [...].
42883974.title: Special Issue: Cell Signaling and Molecular Pathology of Retinal Diseases: 2nd Edition.

42884126.abstract: NADPH-dependent retinol dehydrogenase 12 (RDH12) reduces all-trans-retinal in photoreceptor inner segments to regulate the phototransduction cascade and control the concentration of retinoids in the retina. Variants in RDH12 have been reported to cause an array of retinal disease phenotypes, including autosomal recessive (AR) Leber congenital amaurosis (LCA), a severe form of childhood blindness, and autosomal dominant (AD) retinitis pigmentosa (RP), a milder late-onset rod-dominant disease. Animal models have failed to recapitulate the clinical phenotype; hence, we generated human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC) derived retinal organoids (RO) from a patient with homozygous missense variant c.619A>G p.(Asn207Asp) in RDH12 (RDH12-AR), a patient with heterozygous c.759del p.(Phe254Leufs*24) (RDH12-AD), and an unaffected control. RDH12-AR ROs develop shortened rod and cone photoreceptors (from the outer limiting membrane to the tip of the outer segment), which lack RDH12 localisation in the inner segment. Bulk transcriptomic analysis revealed cone marker and apoptosis dysregulation in RDH12-AR ROs compared to unaffected controls, but phospholipid transport is perturbed in RDH12-AR ROs compared to RDH12-AD. Our study helps to decipher the distinct disease pathways involved in RDH12 retinopathies; however, further modelling from additional patients with isogenic controls will strengthen the findings and aid identification of targets for therapeutic approaches.
42884126.authors: Méjécase C, Toualbi L, Zhou Y et al.
42884126.title: Autosomal Recessive RDH12-Leber Congenital Amaurosis Retinal Organoids Suggest Phospholipid Pathway Dysregulation.

42887780.abstract: Retinal degeneration leads to extensive remodeling of inner retinal circuits following photoreceptor loss, but the intrinsic membrane properties of surviving bipolar cells remain incompletely understood. Here, we investigated the expression and functional contribution of hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated (HCN) channels in ON-bipolar cells using the rd10 mouse model of retinitis pigmentosa. High-resolution fluorescence in situ hybridization showed no significant differences in Hcn1, Hcn2, and Hcn4 transcript levels between wild-type (WT) and rd10 bipolar cells. Whole-cell patch-clamp recordings detected hyperpolarization-activated inward currents consistent with Ih in both WT and rd10 ON-bipolar cells with no significant differences. In current-clamp recordings, the recovery of membrane potential following hyperpolarizing current pulses was significantly slowed by HCN channel blockers (ivabradine and ZD7288) in both genotypes. These findings indicate that HCN-sensitive conductances contribute to membrane potential recovery in ON-bipolar cells and remain detectable after photoreceptor degeneration.
42887780.authors: Chu JW, Kang B, Kim K et al.
42887780.title: Hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated channels preserve excitability in ON-bipolar cells after degeneration.

42890415.abstract: We present a fully automatic algorithm to segment the ellipsoid zone (EZ) on optical coherence tomography (OCT) images of retinitis pigmentosa (RP). We introduce Diffusion Projection U-Net (DPUN), a method to generate en face EZ maps from 3D OCT scans by leveraging diffusion models' state-of-the-art generative capabilities. We further propose Central Annotation Propagation (CAP), a semi-automatic approach that incorporates the segmentation of the central scan to segment all scans in a volume using a memory-reading paradigm. We demonstrated the effectiveness of our methods on a dataset consisting of 60 eyes from 60 participants enrolled in an international, multicenter, phase 3 RP clinical trial (NCT05537220) imaged with spectral-domain OCT at the baseline visit. DPUN outperformed all comparison methods for fully automatic segmentation. DPUN-CAP, which utilized central annotations, achieved the best performance of all models evaluated. The proposed methods produced measurements that were consistent with manual measurements of the EZ area, highlighting their potential utility for clinical trials in which EZ area is a key anatomic endpoint and for monitoring EZ loss progression and treatment response in clinical practice.
42890415.authors: Choy KC, Jaffe GJ, Farsiu S
42890415.title: Diffusion model with central annotation propagation for segmentation of ellipsoid zone maps on OCT scans of retinitis pigmentosa.

42891053.abstract: Aim: Olfactory ensheathing cells (OECs) are commonly utilized in cell-based therapies for neurodegenerative diseases and central nervous system injuries, due to their unique properties of suppressing gliosis and providing neuroprotection. Small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) have emerged as promising therapeutic agents. This study aimed to investigate OEC-sEVs' effect on retinal degeneration. Methods: Proteomics analysis identified differentially expressed proteins between OEC-sEVs and OECs. We conducted subretinal injection of OEC-sEVs and assessed their protective mechanisms in degenerative retina. Real-time quantitative PCR and Western blot were used to detect the expression of phagocytosis-related molecules in retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) cells. Results: Proteomics analysis revealed that proteins enriched in OEC-sEVs were associated with phagocytosis. Following injection into the subretinal spaces of Royal College of Surgeons (RCS) rats, OEC-sEVs were internalized by RPE cells, leading to the transient upregulation of tyrosine-protein kinase Mer (MerTK), activation of the downstream phosphoinositide 3-kinase/Akt signaling pathway, and restoration of the phagocytic activity of RPE cells towards the photoreceptor outer segments. This delayed photoreceptor degeneration, thereby improving retinal function in RCS rats. In the ARPE-19 cell line treated with the specific MerTK inhibitor UNC2881, enhanced phagocytosis of fluorescent particles and porcine photoreceptor outer segments was observed following OEC-sEV internalization. Conclusion: OEC-sEVs were abundant in proteins associated with phagocytosis, which may partially compensate for the phagocytic deficit of the RPE cells observed in a retinitis pigmentosa rat model via the MerTK-related signaling pathway.
42891053.authors: Chen S, Lin X, Cha Z et al.
42891053.journal: Extracellular vesicles and circulating nucleic acids
42891053.title: Olfactory ensheathing cell-derived extracellular vesicles protect the degenerated retinal pigment epithelium by delivering phagocytosis-related proteins.

42893897.abstract: BACKGROUND: Mutations in the cone-rod homeobox (CRX) gene cause dominantly inherited retinopathies with striking phenotypic variability. We define the clinical spectrum and molecular mechanism of a Class III CRX frameshift variant (c.590del, p.(Pro197Argfs*22); CRXP197Rfs) segregating in a four-generation family. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Six family members underwent genetic testing by a retinal dystrophy panel with Sanger confirmation. Carriers received longitudinal phenotyping, including visual acuity, fundus autofluorescence, optical coherence tomography (OCT), and full-field electroretinography (ffERG). Variant function was assessed by rhodopsin-promoter reporter assays in HEK293 cells and Crx-/- mouse retinal explants. RESULTS: Three carriers shared the identical variant yet showed cone-rod dystrophy in variable severity and adult-onset ages. The proband developed progressive central vision loss, nyctalopia, outer-retinal atrophy, and reduced ffERG responses. Two carriers remained asymptomatic with preserved acuity and normal ffERG, exhibiting only mild outer nuclear layer thinning and abnormal autofluorescence. CRXP197Rfs lacked transactivation activity and suppressed wild-type CRX function in a dose-dependent manner. CONCLUSIONS: CRXP197Rfs is a dominant-negative allele that produces cone-rod dystrophy with variable intrafamilial phenotypes. These findings caution against genotype-based prognostication and support mutant-allele knockdown with gene augmentation as therapeutic strategies.
42893897.authors: Gomes IVY, Sun C, Zhang X et al.
42893897.title: Phenotypic variability of a dominant CRX mutation and molecular insights into pathogenesis.

42897362.abstract: Pattern electroretinography (PERG) is a non-invasive test of macular and retinal ganglion cell function, but its low amplitude and inter-subject variability limit its diagnostic use. This study compares three representations of the transient PERG waveform for the detection of six retinal and optic nerve conditions - Birdshot chorioretinopathy, cone-rod dystrophy, hereditary optic atrophy, macular dystrophy, retinitis pigmentosa and Stargardt disease - against healthy controls, using the publicly available PERG-IOBA dataset. A total of 672 recordings from 336 examinations of 304 participants were preprocessed in six stages, and three representations were evaluated under one identical protocol: the raw 255-point amplitude-preserving waveform; 60 engineered clinical, spectral, wavelet and complexity descriptors; and a hybrid representation of 343 variables combining both, with multi-wavelet features from db4, sym2 and coif3. Performance was estimated by 10 × 5-fold participant-grouped cross-validation, in which both eyes and all repeat visits of an individual were kept in the same partition, with nested hyperparameter selection and all data-derived preprocessing fitted inside each training fold. Under the pre-specified primary classifier, the raw waveform gave the highest pooled out-of-fold AUC in four of the six classes (0.906 in cone-rod dystrophy, 0.842 in retinitis pigmentosa, 0.755 in macular dystrophy, 0.673 in hereditary optic atrophy) and the engineered descriptors in the remaining two (0.803 in Stargardt disease, 0.657 in Birdshot chorioretinopathy). The hybrid representation was highest in none, falling below the raw waveform in five of six classes by 0.002 to 0.018, and no non-linear classifier showed a hybrid advantage above 0.006 in mean AUC. A sensitivity analysis identified what does matter: removing the absolute amplitude scale by per-signal z-scoring cost the raw representation 0.055 AUC on average but the engineered descriptors only 0.023, and reversed the ordering of the three representations. Engineered descriptors did not improve on the waveform, but they made the problem tractable for linear models, which gained 0.128 in mean AUC from the reduction in dimensionality. These internally validated findings indicate that absolute PERG amplitude should be preserved rather than normalised away; participant-independent, multi-centre validation is required before clinical application.
42897362.authors: Aygün AB, Açıkgöz R, Coşkun M et al.
42897362.title: Comparison of raw-signal, feature-based and hybrid representations for machine-learning classification of retinal diseases from pattern electroretinography.

42898535.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To describe ophthalmic phenotypes prompting genetic testing and to calculate the molecular diagnostic yield retrospectively in a real-world tertiary health center cohort. METHODS: This retrospective observational study employed a phenotype-first review of archived clinical genetic testing records. Unique individuals with documented ocular manifestations were identified and deduplicated using demographic and phenotype consistency rather than laboratory patient number alone. Patients were assigned one primary molecular outcome: Phenotype-concordant pathogenic or likely pathogenic diagnosis, candidate/variant of uncertain significance/partial finding, unresolved, or secondary/non-diagnostic pathogenic or likely pathogenic finding. Variants of uncertain significance, single pathogenic alleles for recessive disorders, and unphased biallelic variants were not counted as definitive diagnoses. RESULTS: Among 33 unique individuals, phenotype-concordant molecular diagnoses were established in 18.2% (6/33), while candidate, variant of uncertain significance, or partial findings were more frequent at 54.5% (18/33). Diagnoses involved REEP6, TYR, PTEN, BRPF1, and CACNA1F. An additional patient with albinism carried two heterozygous TYR pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants, but phase was not established; confirmation in trans would increase the yield to 21.2%. Excluding a CACNA1F case with a nonspecific archived phenotype reduced the yield to 15.2%. CONCLUSION: The conservative molecular diagnostic yield was 18.2%, with candidate and partial findings substantially outnumbering definitive diagnoses. This gap underscores the importance of phenotype concordance, inheritance-aware interpretation, and segregation analysis in real-world ophthalmic genetics, where unresolved cases represent a reanalysis cohort rather than a diagnostic dead end.
42898535.title: Molecular Diagnostic Yield and Genotype-Phenotype Spectrum of Inherited Eye Diseases in a Tertiary Health Center in Türkiye.

42899905.abstract: Cuproptosis is a recently described copper-dependent form of regulated cell death linked to mitochondrial metabolism, but its relevance to retinal degeneration in retinitis pigmentosa is unknown. Here, we investigated whether cuproptosis-associated changes occur in the retina of the rd10 mouse model of retinitis pigmentosa and whether copper chelation confers neuroprotection. Cuproptosis-associated changes were assessed by measuring retinal copper accumulation, dihydrolipoamide S-acetyltransferase oligomerization, and iron-sulfur cluster protein expression. The copper chelator D-penicillamine was delivered by intravitreal injection, and treatment effects were evaluated using retinal histology, electroretinography, and visually guided behavioral assays. Degenerating rd10 retinas exhibited increased copper accumulation, enhanced dihydrolipoamide S-acetyltransferase oligomerization, and reduced iron-sulfur cluster-associated proteins, consistent with activation of cuproptosis-associated pathways. D-penicillamine attenuated these molecular changes, improved mitochondrial protein markers, and significantly preserved photoreceptor structure. Functional benefit was detectable in light perception behavior, although electroretinographic and optomotor responses were not significantly restored. The copper exporter ATPase copper transporting β was upregulated at an early stage but reduced during peak degeneration, whereas the copper importer copper transporter 1 increased at the later stage, suggesting dynamic copper dyshomeostasis. These findings identify cuproptosis-associated molecular changes as a feature of photoreceptor degeneration in rd10 mice and demonstrate that copper chelation provides structural neuroprotection.
42899905.authors: Li ZY, Li Y, Yang D et al.
42899905.title: Cuproptosis-associated retinal degeneration in a mouse model of retinitis pigmentosa and neuroprotection by copper chelation.

42901316.abstract: Historically, the main operation for cataract was couching, and the interior of the living eye could not be examined until Hermann von Helmholtz introduced the ophthalmoscope in 1851. Since the mid-twentieth century, seven advances have reshaped ophthalmic care. Harold Ridley implanted the first intraocular lens in 1949, and the ophthalmologist Charles Kelman and the engineer Anton Banko developed phacoemulsification, reported in 1967. Robert Machemer performed the first pars plana vitrectomy in 1970, while David Huang and colleagues described optical coherence tomography in 1991. Endothelial keratoplasty, developed by Gerrit Melles and others between 1998 and 2006, replaced only the failing corneal endothelium instead of the full thickness of the cornea. Anti-VEGF therapy followed the purification of VEGF by Napoleone Ferrara and colleagues in 1989 and the approval of ranibizumab in 2006. Minimally invasive glaucoma surgery has spread since 2012, and in 2017 voretigene neparvovec became the first approved gene therapy for an inherited retinal disease. Five of these advances enabled a new type of intervention, whereas endothelial keratoplasty and minimally invasive glaucoma surgery made existing operations safer. For each advance we summarize the best available evidence of benefit to patients and its certainty, which is high for some, such as anti-VEGF therapy, and low for others, such as the effect of imaging on patient outcomes. Each advance created new burdens, from chronic injections to dependence on donor tissue, and routine adoption depended on manufacturing, regulation, cost, reimbursement, and health-system capacity.
42901316.authors: Zhang X, Li F, Huang D et al.
42901316.journal: Progress in retinal and eye research
42901316.title: Mastering the eye: Clinical paradigm shifts from optical restoration to genomic correction.

42904883.title: The First 40 Years of Molecular Ophthalmology Part One: Inherited Retinal Disease: The 2026 Friedenwald Lecture.

42905171.abstract: The Bardet-Biedl syndrome (BBS) is a genetically determined multiorgan disorder characterized by congenital postaxial polydactyly, obesity, hyperphagia and retinal dystrophy that develops in childhood. The condition is heterogeneous both in terms of molecular genetics and clinically: it is caused by mutations in at least 26 genes, and the variable extraocular manifestations include developmental delay, diabetes mellitus and fatty liver. The retinal dystrophy is also heterogeneous and presents with a broad phenotypic spectrum. While there is no specific treatment option for the retinal dystrophy, an approved treatment exists for the hyperphagia-related obesity. In addition to primary care, BBS patients should receive interdisciplinary care at specialized centers. Since 2026, patients with BBS1-associated retinal dystrophy are being enrolled in an ocular gene therapy study to evaluate the preliminary safety and tolerability of AXV-101. Das Bardet-Biedl-Syndrom (BBS) ist eine genetisch bedingte Multiorganerkrankung mit den charakteristischen Merkmalen einer angeborenen postaxialen Polydaktylie, Adipositas, Hyperphagie und in der Kindheit auftretenden Netzhautdystrophie. Die Erkrankung ist sowohl klinisch als auch molekulargenetisch heterogen: Sie wird verursacht durch Mutationen in mindestens 26 Genen und die variablen extraokulären Manifestationen schließen beispielsweise eine Entwicklungsverzögerung, einen Diabetes mellitus und eine Leberverfettung ein. Die Netzhautdystrophie zeigt ebenfalls ein breites phänotypisches Spektrum. Aktuell gibt es zwar keine therapeutische Möglichkeit zur Behandlung der Netzhautdystrophie, aber eine zugelassene Therapie zur Behandlung der hyperphagiebedingten Adipositas. BBS-Patienten sollten zusätzlich zur Primärversorgung in spezialisierten Zentren interdisziplinär betreut werden. Seit 2026 werden Patienten mit BBS1-assoziierter Netzhautdystrophie in eine okuläre Gentherapiestudie eingeschlossen.
42905171.authors: Kühlewein L, Kellner U, Jägle H et al.
42905171.title: [Bardet-Biedl syndrome-diagnosis, care and treatment approaches].

42906929.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Professional societies often serve as a hub for research advances and treatment expertise. As the field of ocular genetics rapidly expands, with the advent of gene-based diagnostics and emerging therapies for inherited retinal diseases, we sought to understand whether the worldwide geographic distribution of professionally affiliated ocular genetics physicians allows for equitable access to this service. METHODS: We evaluated the geographic distribution of physicians affiliated with the International Society for Genetic Eye Disease and Retinoblastoma (ISGEDR), a major professional society for ocular genetics specialists, against the estimated prevalence of retinitis pigmentosa (RP), the most common inherited retinal disease. RESULTS: Across 37 countries, we identified 185 ISGEDR-affiliated physicians, with 47% located in North America and 31% in Europe, while large regions of Africa, Asia, South America, and the Middle East had no ISGEDR physicians. Among represented countries, estimated RP patient-to-physician ratios varied more than 400-fold and increased significantly with larger land area and lower national income. In the United States, 46% of states lacked an ISGEDR physician, and RP burden among represented states varied more than 40-fold, increasing significantly with larger land area. Voronoi mapping of the contiguous United States demonstrated substantial variation in catchment size, with the largest expected travel-burden regions in the Mountain West. DISCUSSION: These findings reveal substantial geographic inequities in the distribution of ISGEDR-affiliated ocular genetics physicians relative to RP burden. This under-representation may reflect a shortage of ocular genetics physicians and/or barriers to professional affiliation within identified regions, suggesting a need for more scalable models of ocular genetics care.
42906929.authors: Dogra N, Perkins J, Levin AV
42906929.title: Geographic disparities in the distribution of ISGEDR-affiliated ocular genetics physicians relative to retinitis pigmentosa burden.

42909590.abstract: PURPOSE: To investigate the genetic and phenotypic spectrum of IMPG2-associated retinopathy in a Korean population. METHODS: This retrospective multicenter study included patients with genetically confirmed IMPG2-associated retinopathy from four institutions in Korea. Comprehensive clinical features, including visual acuity, fundus appearance, and OCT findings were analyzed. Genetic testing was performed using targeted next-generation sequencing panels or whole-exome sequencing. The identified variants were classified according to ACMG guidelines to determine their pathogenicity. RESULTS: Fourteen patients (11 males, 3 females; mean age, 41.4 ± 22.6 years) were included. Thirteen exhibited bilateral involvement. Clinical diagnoses comprised adult-onset vitelliform macular dystrophy (n = 7), retinitis pigmentosa (n = 6), and atypical macular dystrophy characterized by subtle, multifocal photoreceptor alterations (n = 1). Splicing variants at the exon 7-8 junction (c.828+1G>A, c.829-2_829-1delAG) and a splice acceptor variant at exon 9 (c.909-2A>T) were identified in 12 of 14 patients (85.7%), with c.828+1G>A being the most frequent (8/14, 57.1%). 84.2% of the identified variants and 92.9% of the patients harbored loss-of-function mutations, including splicing, frameshift, and nonsense variants. CONCLUSION: Loss-of-function of IMPG2, including haploinsufficiency, appears to play a major role in IMPG2-associated retinopathy. The predominance and clustering of splice-site variants around the exon 7-8 junction may reflect a founder effect and regional sequence susceptibility.
42909590.authors: Song SH, Jeon S, Chung H et al.
42909590.journal: Graefe's archive for clinical and experimental ophthalmology = Albrecht von Graefes Archiv fur klinische und experimentelle Ophthalmologie
42909590.title: Predominance and clustering of splice-site variants in Koreans with IMPG2-associated retinopathy: implications for haploinsufficiency and loss of function as disease mechanisms.

42910815.title: Erratum in: RPGRORF15 Mutations Disrupt Lysosomal Lipid Metabolism in Retinal Pigment Epithelium Cells and Cause Retinitis Pigmentosa.

42913796.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Subretinal adeno-associated virus (AAV) gene delivery is being investigated for retinitis pigmentosa (RP), yet functional efficacy, retinal structural effects, and delivery-associated safety remain uncertain. We synthesised clinical evidence across these outcomes. METHODS: Six databases were searched through January 2026, with an update on September 28, 2026. Random-effects meta-analyses evaluated subretinal AAV gene augmentation; mechanistically distinct therapies were synthesised narratively. Outcomes included microperimetry, best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), full-field stimulus threshold (FST), retinal thickness, and adverse events. Follow-up and sensitivity analyses explored variability. RESULTS: Thirteen reports representing 12 studies were included; eight contributed quantitative data. Microperimetry improved by 6.72 dB (95% CI 6.45-6.98; four studies; I2 = 0%), with most observed gains within six months. Time-stratified sensitivity estimates ranged from 2.77 dB at one month to 6.79 dB at 12 months, without establishing within-patient trajectories. BCVA improved by 4.12 ETDRS letters (95% CI 3.45-4.80; four studies; I2 = 0%), below a conventional five-letter benchmark. Exploratory meta-regression suggested greater acuity gains with follow-up (0.27 letters/month), but cluster-robust inference was nonsignificant (p = 0.10). FST did not improve in two studies. Central retinal thickness decreased by 33.7 μm from baseline (95% CI -37.3 to -30.1; three studies), without establishing treatment-attributable thinning. Ocular adverse events occurred in 29.4% (95% CI 19.1-42.5%), and serious adverse events in 19.4% (95% CI 12.8-28.2%). Small early-phase cohorts, heterogeneous comparators, and insufficient delivery-specific comparisons constrained interpretation. CONCLUSION: Subretinal AAV augmentation showed preliminary functional signals, but clinically meaningful benefit and structural safety remain uncertain. Controlled studies should standardize endpoints and clarify vector-, dose-, and procedure-related risks.
42913796.authors: Chen KY, Chan HC, Chan CM
42913796.journal: Journal of controlled release : official journal of the Controlled Release Society
42913796.title: Functional response, retinal structure and safety of subretinal gene augmentation in retinitis pigmentosa: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

42919695.abstract: Nonsense mutations account for approximately 20% of pathogenic variants in inherited retinal diseases (IRDs). With advances in gene therapy, nucleic acid-based nonsense suppression strategies, including suppressor tRNAs, RNA pseudouridylation, and adenosine-to-inosine RNA editing, have demonstrated therapeutic potential in preclinical studies. These next-generation approaches offer substantial opportunities for engineering and optimization, with the potential to enable precise and efficient restoration of full-length functional proteins. In this review, we propose that IRDs represent an attractive group of diseases for the clinical translation of these next-generation therapies owing to their high burden of nonsense mutations and the unique advantages of ocular gene therapy. We further outline key strategies to accelerate clinical translation, spanning therapeutic engineering, preclinical validation, and mutation-guided clinical trial design.
42919695.authors: Ren C, Hu C, Hu M et al.
42919695.title: Rethinking nonsense suppression therapies in inherited retinal diseases.

42923505.abstract: INTRODUCTION: USH2A-related Usher syndrome type 2A is classically characterized by congenital or early-onset sensorineural hearing loss and later-onset retinitis pigmentosa, and epilepsy is not a recognized feature of USH2A-related disease. CASE PRESENTATION: We report an 11-year-old boy who initially presented with nocturnal focal seizures and left occipital epileptiform discharges, followed by cognitive and academic decline and an electroencephalographic evolution consistent with developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with spike-wave activation in sleep (EE-SWAS). Brain magnetic resonance imaging, including repeat evaluation with 3-Tesla imaging, was normal. Because of known parental consanguinity and a treatment-resistant course, exome sequencing was performed and identified a homozygous pathogenic USH2A variant, USH2A(NM_206933.4):c.802G>A;p.(Gly268Arg), with heterozygous segregation in both parents. Genotype-directed evaluation confirmed bilateral moderate-to-moderately severe sensorineural hearing loss (pure tone average: right 60 dB HL; left 50 dB HL), whereas retinal involvement was not clinically evident at the time of assessment. CONCLUSION: To our knowledge, the co-occurrence of biallelic USH2A pathogenicity and an EE-SWAS phenotype has not been reported previously. However, because the same USH2A variant has not been associated with epilepsy or EE-SWAS in the published literature, this co-occurrence is most plausibly interpreted as a coincidental dual diagnosis/dual pathology. This case is noteworthy because it illustrates that exome sequencing may uncover unexpected but clinically actionable syndromic diagnoses and guide targeted audiologic and ophthalmologic surveillance planning, even when the presenting phenotype is primarily neurologic.
42923505.authors: Gazeteci Tekin H, Kuşgöz F, Cinleti T et al.
42923505.title: Usher Syndrome Type 2A and Epileptic Encephalopathy with Spike-Wave Activation in Sleep: A Coincidental Dual Diagnosis? Case Report.

42923813.abstract: In order to systematically evaluate the efficacy and safety of topical carbonic anhydrase inhibitors (CAIs) in the treatment of macular edema across different retinal disorders, a systematic review was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to June 13, 2026, without language or publication date restrictions. Clinical studies evaluating topical dorzolamide or brinzolamide for macular edema of any etiology were included. Data regarding study characteristics, treatment protocols, visual and anatomical outcomes, and follow-up were extracted independently by two reviewers. Twenty-eight studies met the inclusion criteria, comprising randomized controlled trials, quasi-experimental studies, cohort studies, case series, and one analytical cross-sectional study. Overall, the included studies were of moderate-to-high methodological quality. Retinitis pigmentosa-associated cystoid macular edema was the most frequently investigated condition (13 studies), followed by X-linked retinoschisis (10 studies), diabetic macular edema (four studies), and one macular edema following vitrectomy and epiretinal membrane removal. Topical dorzolamide was the most commonly evaluated agent, whereas topical brinzolamide was investigated less frequently. Across retinal disorders, topical CAIs consistently reduced central macular thickness and improved retinal morphology as assessed by optical coherence tomography. Functional outcomes were more variable, with improvements in best-corrected visual acuity observed primarily in selected patients with retinitis pigmentosa and diabetic macular edema, whereas visual gains were generally modest in X-linked retinoschisis. Long-term studies reported recurrence of macular edema despite continued treatment, particularly in retinitis pigmentosa. Topical CAIs were well tolerated, with no serious ocular or systemic adverse events reported. Topical CAIs provide consistent anatomical improvement in macular edema, particularly in inherited retinal disorders, while functional benefits are less predictable. This discrepancy between anatomical and functional outcomes may be attributed to prolonged photoreceptor loss, retinal pigment epithelium dysfunction, and irreversible disruption of the ellipsoid zone. Their favorable safety profile and non-invasive administration support their use as a therapeutic option, especially for retinitis pigmentosa-associated cystoid macular edema and selected cases of X-linked retinoschisis and diabetic macular edema. However, the current evidence is limited by predominantly observational studies and clinical heterogeneity. Well-designed multicenter randomized controlled trials are needed to establish their optimal role in the management of macular edema.
42923813.authors: Sadr A, Maleki A, Asadollahi M et al.
42923813.title: Topical Carbonic Anhydrase Inhibitors in Macular Edema: A Systematic Review.

42924989.abstract: PURPOSE: RP is the most common inherited retinal dystrophy. Limited understanding of how diverse genetic defects converge to cause photoreceptor degeneration hinders the development of mutation-agnostic therapies. Although intracellular Ca²⁺ dysregulation is an early hallmark across genetic variants, its mechanistic link to photoreceptor degeneration remains unclear. This study investigated whether plasma membrane calcium ATPases (PMCA)-mediated Ca²⁺ extrusion induces cytoplasmic acidification that contributes to photoreceptor death in two mouse models of RP. METHODS: PMCA expression (immunofluorescence, RT-qPCR), cytoplasmic acidification (LysoTracker Red [LTR] staining), ultrastructural changes (electron microscopy), calpain-2 activity (in situ zymography) and cell death (TUNEL) were assessed in RP mouse retinas. PMCA-mediated acidification was validated in wild-type (WT) retinal explants under ionophore-induced Ca²⁺ overload. Neuroprotection by PMCA inhibition was evaluated ex vivo (retinal explants) and in vivo (intravitreal injection) by histological photoreceptor preservation. RESULTS: Retinas from rd10 and homozygous P23H mice exhibited cytoplasmic acidification respect to WT. During the early stages of degeneration, the proportion of acidified photoreceptors (LTR-positive) exceeded that of TUNEL-positive photoreceptors, with LTR staining appearing before the onset of TUNEL labeling. Acidification correlated with PMCA upregulation. Ionophore-induced Ca²⁺ overload recapitulated cytoplasmic acidification ex vivo in WT retinas, which was prevented by PMCA inhibition. In rd10 mice, PMCA inhibition preserved photoreceptors ex and in vivo at different stages. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings identify PMCA as a key mediator of pathological cytoplasmic acidification in RP and improve understanding of mechanisms underlying photoreceptor degeneration, which may facilitate the development of mutation-independent therapies and stage-specific interventions for RP progression.
42924989.authors: Hernández-Pinto AM, Rodríguez-Muela N, Pimentel-Mayordomo N et al.
42924989.title: Plasma Membrane Calcium ATPases Drive Cytoplasmic Acidification and Photoreceptor Degeneration in Retinitis Pigmentosa.

42926372.abstract: Retinitis pigmentosa (RP) is genetically heterogeneous, yet initiating mutations converge on primary rod degeneration followed by cone dysfunction and loss. Activated microglia are implicated in this secondary phase, but whether selective immunometabolic reprogramming of microglia preserves retinal function remains unknown. In human iPSC-derived microglia and retinal CD11b+ cells, PGC1α induction suppressed LPS-driven interferon signaling and cytokine release, yet Seahorse analysis and isotopologue tracing showed that energy metabolism remained altered. We therefore fused PGC1α to a multivalent p65-HSF1 module, yielding ~2.5-fold higher nuclear receptor output than native PGC1α and coordinated engagement of oxidative and anti-inflammatory programs in mouse retinal CD11b+ cells. Microglia-restricted expression in humanized RHO P347L mice preserved photopic responses through six months, increased retinal thickness and promoted ramified subretinal IBA1+ morphology. Microglial immunometabolism thus represents a potentially genotype-independent neuroprotective target in RP, and engineered PGC1α co-activators provide a means to sustain oxidative metabolism under inflammatory pressure.
42926372.authors: Winogrodzki T, Hernandez-Reyes J, Solanky R et al.
42926372.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
42926372.title: A synthetic PGC1α co-activator reprograms microglial immunometabolism to preserve cone function in retinal degeneration.

42927157.abstract: Bilateral multifocal serous retinal pigment epithelial detachment (PED) is uncommon, and its coexistence with generalized retinal dysfunction has rarely been reported. We report a 55-year-old man referred for bilateral fundus abnormalities who complained of a paracentral scotoma, photophobia, and nyctalopia. Best-corrected visual acuity was 20/16 in the right eye and 20/13 in the left eye. Fundus examination revealed numerous transparent, round serous PEDs distributed from the posterior pole to the equator in both eyes, with retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) atrophy adjacent to the vascular arcades. Optical coherence tomography showed multiple PEDs with hyporeflective lumens and outer retinal atrophy sparing the fovea. Fundus autofluorescence demonstrated hyperautofluorescent PED margins and hypoautofluorescent atrophic areas. Full-field electroretinogram (ERG) revealed severely reduced to non-recordable rod and combined rod-cone responses, with markedly reduced and delayed cone and 30-Hz flicker responses; Goldmann perimetry demonstrated bilateral ring scotomas. These findings indicated generalized rod-cone dysfunction resembling retinitis pigmentosa (RP). An extensive infectious and inflammatory workup was unremarkable, and no etiology was identified. The patient was managed conservatively and remained stable over two years of observation. This report documents a rare coexistence of bilateral multifocal serous PED and generalized rod-cone dysfunction resembling RP, characterized by multimodal imaging, full-field ERG, and Goldmann perimetry.
42927157.authors: Fukagai H, Nariya Y, Sugimoto K et al.
42927157.title: Bilateral Multifocal Serous Retinal Pigment Epithelial Detachments Coexisting With Generalized Rod-Cone Dysfunction Resembling Retinitis Pigmentosa.

42927978.abstract: Luxturna® (voretigene neparvovec-rzyl) for RPE65-associated retinal dystrophy was the first FDA-approved in vivo gene therapy and, 9 years later, remains the only approved retinal gene therapy. A search of clinicaltrials.gov identified 80 interventional phase 1-3 U.S. studies using AAV vectors, 45 using subretinal injection (SRI), and 33 using intravitreal injection (IVT). SRI efficiently transduces photoreceptors and RPE but transduces only the detached retinal area and carries procedure-related risks. IVT provides broader exposure and avoids retinal detachment but has shown limited efficacy for retinal targets and may produce dose-dependent inflammation. Overall, 11.6% of eyes in peer-reviewed publications receiving gene therapy via SRI experienced serious adverse events (SAEs); and in some studies, 100% experienced treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs). The gap between an active clinical pipeline and regulatory success raises the question: how does route of administration interact with therapeutic biology and clinical trial design? X-linked retinitis pigmentosa (XLRP) due to RPGR variants illustrates this challenge. Nine of 10 trials treating RPGR-related XLRP used SRI, with microperimetry and low light visual acuity as efficacy endpoints; 2 completed phase 2/3 studies failed to meet their primary endpoints. The XOLARIS XLRP natural history study suggests that other measures (e.g., visual field loss, central ellipsoid zone width) may better capture progression. Thus, retinal gene therapy clinical trial design must match the route of administration to the cellular target, therapeutic mechanism, and disease distribution. Emerging vectors and delivery strategies that expand retinal coverage while reducing procedural injury are critical to improve the likelihood of successful retinal gene therapy trials.
42927978.authors: Marmorstein AD, Beltran WA, Scruggs BA
42927978.journal: Journal of ocular pharmacology and therapeutics : the official journal of the Association for Ocular Pharmacology and Therapeutics
42927978.title: Does Route of Administration Affect the Outcome of Retinal Gene Therapy Clinical Trials?

42929859.abstract: Retinal degenerative diseases, including age-related macular degeneration (AMD), retinitis pigmentosa (RP), and Stargardt disease, represent leading causes of irreversible vision loss worldwide, collectively affecting hundreds of millions of people. Cell-based therapies, particularly those leveraging induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs), retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) transplantation, and CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing, have emerged as promising treatment modalities that may preserve, replace, or partially restore retinal function. However, these approaches face significant challenges in patient stratification, manufacturing consistency, surgical precision, and long-term outcome monitoring. Artificial intelligence (AI), encompassing machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), and computer vision, is increasingly being integrated across the cell therapy pipeline to address these limitations. This review comprehensively explores the role of AI in enhancing cell-based retinal therapies, spanning disease diagnosis and patient selection, stem cell quality control and differentiation optimization, CRISPR off-target detection, retinal organoid characterization, scalable manufacturing, and post-transplantation monitoring through multimodal retinal imaging. Throughout, we distinguish direct retinal cell-therapy evidence from retinal-adjacent, cross-domain, and conceptual evidence. We also propose an AI-powered end-to-end pipeline that connects patient profiling through gene editing, cell production, and transplantation to longitudinal outcomes tracking (a forward-looking framework that needs to be clinically validated in future). While AI offers powerful tools to enhance efficacy, reproducibility, and personalization, it does not replace the clinical and biological foundations of cell therapy. Critical challenges remain, including data scarcity, algorithmic interpretability, regulatory compliance, and clinical validation. This review concludes that the strategic integration of AI has plausible potential to become supportive infrastructure for scalable and reproducible cell-based treatments for retinal diseases, although its necessity has not been demonstrated and prospective clinical validation is still required, and biological insight and rigorous empirical verification remain fundamental.
42929859.authors: Srivastava GK, Shukla P, Millas SC et al.
42929859.title: Artificial Intelligence as a Catalyst for Cell-Based Therapies in Retinal Disease.

42931621.abstract: Retinitis pigmentosa (RP) is the most common inherited retinal dystrophy and remains largely untreatable. This review summarizes RP pathogenesis and critically appraises emerging therapeutic strategies, including gene augmentation, gene editing, RNA-based therapies, gene-agnostic and neuroprotective approaches, stem-cell therapy and their delivery platforms. We compare these strategies according to mutation mechanism, disease stage, durability, delivery route, and current level of clinical evidence. Although several approaches have shown improved structural and functional outcomes in preclinical and early-phase studies, RPE65-directed gene augmentation (voretigen neparvovec) remains the only approved therapy, and even it does not halt degeneration. For most modalities, long-term efficacy, safety, durability and clinical validation are not yet established, and translation is further constrained by delivery, immunogenicity, manufacturing, and cost. Rather than a realized paradigm shift, current evidence points to a rapidly advancing but still largely investigational field with successful clinical translation remaining elusive.
42931621.authors: Tuli N, Baeshen M, Echbicheb M et al.
42931621.title: Retinitis Pigmentosa: A Review of Its Pathogenesis and Emerging Molecular and Cellular Therapies.

42941794.abstract: The study purpose was to assess the diagnostic value of whole-genome sequencing (WGS) in identifying candidate genetic variants in patients with inherited retinal diseases (IRDs). We investigated 107 unrelated Russian patients with retinal diseases who carried single pathogenic variants in any of nine common autosomal recessive IRD genes (ABCA4, USH2A, EYS, CRB1, RPE65, CNGB3, CNGA3, CEP290, and GUCY2D). WGS was performed for all patients; candidate splice variants were functionally validated using minigene assays. The total diagnostic yield was 40.2% (43/107). In 25.2% of cases (27/107), the diagnosis was established by identifying a second variant in one of the following candidate genes: EYS (n = 9), USH2A (n = 8), ABCA4 (n = 5), CNGB3 (n = 3), CRB1 and CEP290 (n = 1 each). In 15.0% of cases (16/107), the diagnosis was reclassified by variants in alternative IRD genes (autosomal dominant, X-linked, mitochondrial, or syndromic). The majority of second variants detected in AR cases were CNVs (55.5%, 15 patients), followed by non-coding variants (26.0%, seven), structural rearrangements (14.8%, four) and exonic point variant (3.7%, one). Two recurrent CNVs were observed: a gross deletion of exons 22-24 in USH2A (n = 4) and a deletion partially affecting exon 19 of EYS (n = 4). Structural variants were mostly represented by delINV rearrangements (n = 5). Minigene assays confirmed that three novel deep intronic variants (in CHM, EYS, and CEP290) and one non-canonical splice-acceptor variant in USH2A which disrupt splicing, causes pseudoexon inclusion with premature termination or in-frame exon skipping respectively. Thus, WGS improves the diagnostic yield in IRDs by detecting variants missed by targeted sequencing, supporting its clinical utility in ophthalmologic practice.
42941794.authors: Ogorodova N, Stepanova A, Geletskaia P et al.
42941794.title: Whole-Genome Sequencing in Diagnostics of Unsolved Cases of Inherited Retinal Diseases.

42941826.abstract: MFRP (Membrane Frizzled-Related Protein) is a member of the frizzled-related family of proteins with currently unknown molecular function in the eye. Mutations in the MFRP gene in humans cause microphthalmia, nanophthalmia, retinitis pigmentosa, and foveoschisis, and are also associated with refractive errors. The clinical presentations among patients with MFRP mutations varies, with some showing one of the abnormalities and others combinations of disease phenotypes, suggesting the action of modifier genes. Unlike genetic studies in humans, localization and eventual identification of modifier genes in mouse models is straightforward. Here we report the chromosomal localization of five novel quantitative trait loci (QTL) affecting the degree of photoreceptor degeneration and axial length in a mouse model carrying the homozygous Mfrprd6 allele. QTL analysis was performed on genotype and phenotype data from 225 F2 progeny homozygous for the Mfrprd6 mutant allele derived from an intercross of (B6.Cg-Mfrprd6/rd6 × C3A.BLiA-Pde6b+/J) F1 mice. Three QTL peaks were detected for number of photoreceptor nuclei, a measure of retinal degeneration, on Chr2 (53.3 centimorgan (cM)), Chr4 (56.6 cM), and Chr12 (45.5 cM). Two QTL were detected for axial length on Chr3 (49.5 cM) and Chr19 (24.5 cM). The results demonstrate that diverse Mfrp-associated disease phenotypes can be genetically modified, indicating that genetic variation underlies phenotypic variation.
42941826.authors: Pinkney J, Weatherly S, Collin GB et al.
42941826.title: Mapping Genetic Modifiers Affecting Photoreceptor Degeneration and Axial Length in Eyes from Homozygous Mfrp(rd6) Mice.

42955009.authors: Valensi J, Shalom S, Sharon D
42955009.title: Essential Kinase C Zeta in Nonsyndromic Retinitis Pigmentosa.

42955015.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Inherited retinal diseases are genetically heterogeneous disorders, with retinitis pigmentosa (RP) representing the most common form; although more than 90 genes have been implicated, many RP cases remain molecularly unsolved. OBJECTIVES: To describe an adult-onset RP phenotype associated with loss-of-function variants in PRKCZ, profile the clinical features of this disorder, and investigate the underlying disease mechanism. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: In this case series study, genomic analyses were performed in individuals with unsolved childhood- and adult-onset retinal disease recruited through international research and diagnostic programs. Detailed clinical characterization was conducted in affected individuals. In vitro analyses were carried out to validate the genomic findings using primary and transduced cell-based experimental approaches. Genomic analyses were performed from October 2023 to December 2025; functional studies were carried out from January 2024 to May 2026. EXPOSURE: Bi-allelic likely pathogenic variants in a novel RP disease gene candidate, PRKCZ. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was genetic, clinical, and functional effects of bi-allelic PRKCZ inactivating variants associated with adult-onset RP. A detailed ophthalmologic assessment was conducted to characterize the clinical phenotype. Functional analyses in patient-derived fibroblasts and transduced cell lines were performed to validate the consequence of disruptive variants on PRKCZ transcript processing and PKCζ function. RESULTS: Among approximately 4500 individuals with unsolved childhood- and adult-onset retinal disease tested, 6 bi-allelic PRKCZ variants were identified in 13 affected individuals from 10 unrelated families, 5 of which were predicted to lead to loss of function (frameshift, nonsense, or splice-altering variants). Six of 13 affected individuals (46%) were female. Most cases carried a recurrent frameshift variant (c.139_140del; p.Met47Valfs*19). All variants selectively affected the long PRKCZ transcript encoding the N-terminal Phox and Bem1 (PB1) domain. Clinically, PRKCZ-associated RP showed adult onset (18-49 years), progressive night blindness, peripheral visual field constriction, and eventual central vision loss. Four individuals exhibited adult-onset sensorineural hearing loss. Functional studies in patient-derived fibroblasts demonstrated selective loss of the long PRKCZ isoform, impaired ciliogenesis, and altered mitochondrial organization, which were validated in stable PRKCZ knockdown cell lines. Structural modeling and coimmunoprecipitation assays indicated that the missense variant was associated with the disruption of PB1 domain-mediated protein-protein interactions. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this case series study, bi-allelic inactivating variants in PRKCZ were associated with adult-onset RP with an isoform-specific mechanism involving the long retinal-enriched transcript. These findings expand the genetic spectrum of RP and highlight PRKCZ as a potentially clinically relevant gene implicated in adult-onset retinal degeneration.
42955015.authors: Cordeddu V, Sangermano R, Mulder SWM et al.
42955015.title: Bi-Allelic PRKCZ Loss-of-Function Variants and Adult-Onset Retinitis Pigmentosa.

42957013.abstract: PURPOSE: This study aimed to describe retinal phenotype, longitudinal clinical course, and genetic findings in Japanese patients with NPHP1-associated Senior-Løken syndrome and their siblings. DESIGN: Retrospective, multicenter case series. PATIENTS AND METHODS: This study included 12 patients with biallelic pathogenic NPHP1 variants, comprising 10 probands with symptomatic retinal dystrophy recruited from six ophthalmic centers across Japan and 2 affected siblings identified through family screening. Clinical and genetic findings were analyzed. Retinal dystrophy was diagnosed using fundus photography, fundus autofluorescence (FAF), optical coherence tomography, and electroretinography. Genetic testing was performed using whole-exome and/or whole-genome sequencing. Follow-up ranged from 0 to 44 years (mean, 14.6 years). MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Retinal phenotype, onset of retinopathy and nephropathy, and genotype. RESULTS: Retinal phenotypes included cone/cone-rod dystrophy (4 patients), retinitis pigmentosa (4 patients), sector retinitis pigmentosa (2 patients), pigmented paravenous retinochoroidal atrophy (1 patient), and normal retina (1 patient). FAF images showed a descending tract in 5 patients. Retinopathy preceded nephropathy in 9 patients, all of whom were initially diagnosed with Leber congenital amaurosis or early-onset retinal dystrophy. Genetic testing showed that 11 patients harbored a homozygous whole-NPHP1 deletion, whereas 1 carried compound heterozygous NPHP1 and EYS variants. CONCLUSIONS: Patients with NPHP1-associated Senior-Løken syndrome showed considerable inter- and intrafamilial variability in retinal phenotype. Pigmented paravenous retinochoroidal atrophy can be associated with NPHP1 variants. A descending tract on FAF imaging may be a characteristic feature of retinal degeneration in Senior-Løken syndrome. Retinopathy, which commonly manifests as Leber congenital amaurosis or early-onset retinal dystrophy, often precedes nephropathy in patients with NPHP1-associated Senior-Løken syndrome.
42957013.authors: Kuniyoshi K, Domoto A, Hayashi T et al.
42957013.title: Retinal phenotypes and longitudinal clinical courses in patients with NPHP1-associated Senior-Løken syndrome.

42957830.abstract: This is a comprehensive review on the progress of laser photocoagulation therapy in the treatment of pediatric retinal diseases. The review begins by introducing the background and characteristics of pediatric retinal diseases, as well as the principles and mechanisms of retinal photocoagulation currently employed in clinical practice. Subsequently, the paper elaborates on the application of laser photocoagulation therapy in pediatric retinal diseases such as Retinopathy of Prematurity (ROP), Familial Exudative Vitreoretinopathy (FEVR), Coats' disease, Norrie disease, Incontinentia Pigmenti (IP), Morning Glory Syndrome (MGS), and Retinitis Pigmentosa (RP). Laser therapy has shown significant efficacy in slowing disease progression, improving visual function, and preventing severe complications. However, laser therapy also carries potential complications that require careful control of laser parameters during treatment. With advancements in technology and further clinical research, our understanding of the application of laser therapy in pediatric retinal diseases has deepened, but further research is needed to refine treatment protocols and enhance treatment effectiveness.
42957830.authors: Zhang Q, Chai X, Gong D et al.
42957830.title: Progress in the application of laser photocoagulation therapy in the treatment of pediatric retinal diseases.

42960537.abstract: BACKGROUND: NMNAT1 variants are a recognized cause of Leber congenital amaurosis (LCA), but NMNAT1-associated early-onset retinal dystrophy (EORD) phenotype remains rarely reported. Standard inherited retinal dystrophy (IRD) gene panel testing is limited in its ability to detect pathogenic non-coding variants, which are systematically excluded from conventional testing. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A 6-year-old female underwent comprehensive ophthalmic examination, followed by a 330 gene IRD panel, whole-genome sequencing (WGS) and parental segregation. RESULTS: The patient presented with nystagmus, esotropia, and reduced visual acuity. Multimodal imaging revealed atypical bilateral maculopathy while full-field ERG responses were borderline. The IRD panel was negative and subsequent WGS identified compound heterozygous NMNAT1 variant, a novel 5'UTR splice donor variant (c.-57 + 1 G > C) and a missense variant (c.480 G > C, p. Leu160Phe) confirmed to be in trans by parental segregation analysis. CONCLUSION: We report a novel NMNAT1 5'UTR splice donor variant in a case of NMNAT1-associated EORD, expanding the genotypic and phenotypic spectrum of NMNAT1 disease. Comprehensive genomic analysis is essential for diagnosing atypical IRD presentations.
42960537.authors: Morales PC, Estrada-Puente C, D'Cunha R et al.
42960537.title: NMNAT1 early-onset retinal dystrophy (EORD) caused by a novel 5'UTR splice donor variant.

42964045.authors: Gu VY, Guo J, Zhang X et al.
42964045.title: Correction: Genetic testing and reproductive decision-making in Chinese families with inherited retinal disease: a cross-sectional study.

42969949.abstract: The human ciliopathy Alström syndrome is caused by mutations in ALMS1. How ALMS1 contributes to cilia function has been unclear. Unlike other ciliopathy-associated proteins, ALMS1 localizes to the proximal end of centrioles, raising the possibility that it contributes to cilia function via a distinct mechanism. We found that, without ALMS1, centrioles are short and frequently break at their proximal ends. Truncated, broken ALMS1 mutant centrioles display reduced microtubule-organizing activity and disrupted centriole linkers. Without ALMS1, Golgi-derived cargos, including transmembrane components of the transition zone, are impaired in their trafficking to the centrosome. Consequently, ALMS1 is important for transition zone assembly, ciliogenesis, and the control of ciliary membrane composition. In mice, disruption of ALMS1 causes progressive, age-dependent loss of cilia in tissues affected in Alström syndrome, including retina, kidney, and brain. We conclude that Alström syndrome is caused by disruption of proximal centriole integrity and centrosome-directed protein trafficking, compromising ciliary assembly and maintenance.
42969949.authors: Phan TP, Derderian C, Herranz-Pérez V et al.
42969949.title: ALMS1 stabilizes the proximal centriole to drive transition zone assembly and ciliogenesis.

42970243.abstract: BACKGROUND: Inherited retinal diseases account for the leading cause of blindness amongst working-age adults in the United Kingdom. The approval of novel therapies for these diseases requires an understanding of how clinical measures of retinal function relate to self-perceived visual disability. This study investigates the association between visual function and quality-of-life in patients with inherited retinal disease, to identify meaningful health outcomes. METHODS: A cross-sectional study (ISRCTN24016133) was conducted in patients with monogenic retinal disease. Vision-related and health-related quality-of-life were assessed using psychometrically validated questionnaires: Visual Function Questionnaire-25 (VFQ-25), Low Luminance Questionnaire (LLQ) and EuroQoL-5D-5L. Visual function measures included best-corrected visual acuity (VA) in ETDRS and Moorfields acuity chart (MAC) letters, low luminance VA (LLVA) and mesopic microperimetry. RESULTS: Twenty-five patients were recruited. The median age was 30 years (interquartile range 23-48) and 80% of patients were male. LLQ scores were lower than VFQ-25 findings and exhibited fewer ceiling and floor effects. Microperimetry was the only significant predictor of VFQ-25 and LLQ scores (p = 0.04, R² = 37% and p = 0.01, R² = 54%, respectively). No significant associations were observed between other visual function measures and questionnaire scores.
